content_html_sanitized:
Posted October 1, 2007 

Analysis by Richard Cowan
Cowan@MarijuanaNews.com   

 

 

About this time every year NORML gets the FBI's Uniform Crime Report and then issues a press release and a more comprehensive report on the number of marijuana arrests in the last year. I then wait one week and call NORML's CEO, Allen St.Pierre, and ask the same question: Did any of the major media outlets report the numbers? 

 

 

Every year, the answer is pretty much the same. NO. 

See 

Arresting Developments: 2003 Cannabis Arrests Hit All-Time High In DEAland, Decline In UK and Canada. Deaths Related to One Drug Soar In Holland. Guess Which One.  

and 

NORML Reports Marijuana Arrests For 2002 Near Record High Pot Smokers Arrested In America At A Rate Of One Every 45 Seconds Plus Analysis by Richard Cowan.  

and 

Dude, You're Getting A Journalism Lesson. The Media Won't Report How Many Cannabis Arrests There Are in DEAland, or New York City, But This Celebrity Arrest Is Even Reported In The Washington Post. 

Democracy, Cannabis and the Drug Czar. Arrests Remain Close to Record Levels. Support for Medical Cannabis Now Up to 80%. And 34% Favor Full Legalization. We Are Winning, But The People Are Suffering.

and one for Giuliani, 

Marijuana Arrests In New York City Continue to Soar. Arrests Will Exceed 60,000 for this Year. Up From Only 720 in 1992!  

This year the number of arrests hit an all-time high of 829,625, which is more than for all violent crimes combined, , including murder, manslaughter, forcible rape, robbery and aggravated assault, but still the major media largely ignored this striking fact. 

 

 

Drug warriors like to claim that no one is going to prison for marijuana, and almost 90% of last year's victims were only charged with possession, which is a misdemeanor in every state. Nonetheless, the consequences of just being arrested can be devastating for some people. 

From 1997 see 

 Are people really being arrested for marijuana possession? What happens when someone is arrested? 

and  

LIFE SENTENCES: COLLATERAL SANCTIONS ASSOCIATED WITH MARIJUANA OFFENSES A report by the Center for Cognitive Liberty & Ethics 

(Ver. 1, published July 2, 2007) 

Of course, none of that is ever reported, even by the supposedly anti-war blogosphere. 

See

Sicko and The Return of MarijuanaNews.com. The Failure of the Left to Address the Drug War. By Richard Cowan. 

With the exception of the megasite, HuffingtonPost.com, which carried an article by NORML's Paul Armentano, and another excellent essay today by Vince Beiser: The Other War We're Losing, the war on cannabis users, medical and otherwise, is still off the left's radar. 

 

Even Salon.com, and Slate.com which once carried excellent articles on the Drug Czar's mendacity, almost never mention the war on us. 

See

Online Magazine Salon.com Documents Hollywood Sell-Out To Drug Czar  

and 

Dan Forbes Documents Walters Lies About Potency. Understanding That The War On Cannabis Is Built On Lies Is Key to Understanding More Than Just Drug War.  

By contrast, Reason magazine has had excellent coverage, especially Radley Balko's all-too-regular reports on Paramilitary Police Raids. Two years ago, even National Review had a great report on marijuana arrests Wrong Drug, Wrong War by Rich Lowry.  

 

 

In 1984, Orwell described Crimestop as a part of a thought process that includes being bored or repelled by any train of thought which is capable of leading in a heretical direction. I think that this term best describes the Left's aversion to criticizing the drug war. After all, any criticism of a government program implies that the nanny state is fallible.  

See

The 50th Anniversary of The Publishing Of Orwells 1984  

Analysis By Richard Cowan  

Or is it that the rights of accused terrorists are more important than the rights of accused medical marijuana users? 

 

 

Perhaps that would explain the next story. 

 

Following the publication of the Institute of Medicine Report (funded by Clinton's Drug Czar, General Barry McCaffrey), the new part line on medical cannabis became No Medicine Is Smoked, and the term for cannabis became smoked marijuana, as in smoked marijuana is not a medicine. 

See

Incestuous Amplification. Prohibitionists Do It with Their Jackboots On, But It Is Not as Much Fun as It Sounds. Analysis by Richard Cowan  
and links. 

Ever since most doctors managed to kick their nicotine addiction, smoking anything is medically incorrect.
See

Health Canada's Office of Cannabis Medical Access' Stakeholder Advisory Committee Includes Physicians for A Smoke Free Canada - Not The Compassion Societies. But It Will Let Them Talk For An Hour  

 

One might think that, given this focus on smoking, the federal government might at least give a low priority to someone making edible products for the medical cannabis market.  

 

However, last week the feds raided Oakland-based Tainted Inc., which made cannabis edibles including candy bars, cookies, marshmallow pies, ice cream, peanut butter, jelly, energy drinks and "Rice Krispy treats." 

 

Tainted's founder, Michael Martin, is now a fugitive, perhaps influenced by the fact that earlier this year, Kenneth Affolter was sentenced to nearly six years in federal prison for a similar crime making Stoney Rancher, Rasta Reese's and Keef Kat.

 

No medicine is eaten. 

 

And for one more absurdity, the LA Times, which still can't bring itself to report on marijuana arrests, did carry one story that indicates they sort of get it.

Crime and the time  

In recent congressional testimony, U.S. District Judge Paul G. Cassell cited the case of Weldon Angelos, whom Cassell was forced by federal mandatory minimum sentences to send to prison for 59 years -- for three $350 marijuana sales, in each instance with a gun in his car. As a comparison, Cassell offered a list of maximum sentences for other crimes:  

 

* Hijacking an aircraft: 24 years, 5 months 

 

* Terrorist bombing in a public place: 19 years, 6 months 

 

* Second-degree murder: 14 years 

 

* Rape of a 10-year-old child: 11 years, 3 months 

 

* Providing weapons to support a foreign terrorist organization: 8 years, 1 month 

 

There is a certain irony to be found in this last item. Mr. Affolters company was called Beyond Bomb. If he had provided a foreign terrorist with a real bomb, he would have been sentenced to just a couple of years more.
